critical_code_review_comments: server.py — RevisionDevelopment Pydantic model + DevelopmentalTheory.revision_development field are cleanly wired: applies defaults False, all seven string fields default empty. The first-draft acceptance ('rd.applies must be False when no prior draft') held on both Session A turn 1 and Session B turn 1, which means the reasoner prompt correctly reads the presence of a prior draft in theory_history rather than the mere existence of a 'revise' kind. This is the right architectural discipline — a client calling kind='writing' on turn 1 will always have applies=false regardless of anything else.

server.py REVISION AS DEVELOPMENT FRAMEWORK prompt block — the growth-vs-superficial discrimination is precise: on the substantive revise ('Social media harms close friendships because constant, shallow contact crowds out the focused attention deep friendship needs') the model returned development_detected='yes — claim moved from vague evaluative...' and named primary_growth='precision and arguability of the controlling claim' with a transfer_message that generalizes the move ("Embedding a 'because' or causal mechanism in a cla..."). On the intensifier-only edit ('bad' -> 'really bad', 'teen' -> 'teenage') the model returned development_detected startswith 'no'/'partial' and populated remaining_opportunity WITHOUT fabricating growth — a fabrication would have been the easy failure mode here. Explicit anti-fabrication discipline in the prompt is working.

server.py edit-counting suppression — across both revise invitations (growth AND superficial), zero of the 8 edit-counting regexes fired (r'you made \\d+ (?:changes|edits|revisions)', r'you revised a lot', r'\\d+ (?:changes|edits|revisions) made', etc.). Revision is being framed as developmental change, not scorekeeping — the M13 core discipline.

server.py _compact_theory — the growth revise on Session A preserved cp.primary='persuade' (M6) + reader_construction.applies=true (M12) + scaffolding_control.primary_target non-empty and singular + instructional_mode='explicit_instruction' + cycle_status='continue' (M11). Adding a seventh framework (M13) did not crowd out prior ones; the M11 orchestrator still selects ONE target per turn. That's tight coordination discipline.

server.py theory_history append semantics — after 'revise', theory_history[0].version=1 with theory body distinct from theory_history[-1] (version>=2). No overwrite; the trajectory is queryable. This is required by the M13 promise 'engine reads revision as developmental growth across drafts'.

server.py M5A boundary — intervention.focus='writing' held on ALL 4 turns; the AI invitation in growth turn 2 did not echo or rewrite the student's exact revised text (verified via 'draft not in invitation' guard). M5A is intact under the new M13 lens.

test infrastructure — the xdist LoadScopeScheduling in /app/backend/pytest.ini runs each test class on one worker sequentially, which is exactly right for a shared-session pattern (Session A turn 1 must run before Session A turn 2 on the same worker to share the sid). This is why the class-scoped session_state fixture pattern in test_milestone13_iteration18.py works end-to-end.

rca of the issue: No functional defect in the app. One test-run failure on the initial parallel run: TestGrowthSessionA::test_a2_revise_growth_triggers_primary_growth_and_transfer FAILED with `AssertionError: turn2 SSE failed: err=None` on 3 back-to-back empty-done SSE frames (status 200 + saw event:done but data-line empty on all 3 attempts). Backend logs show the LLM call did fire and complete on each attempt (LiteLLM completion() model=claude-sonnet-4-6 at 12:43:22, 12:44:23, 12:45:27 — each ~1min elapsed). This is the same transient empty-done SSE frame documented in iteration_16 (M11) and iteration_17 (M12) — the LLM returns a full theory, but the SSE stream from Anthropic through the emergent proxy occasionally drops the payload on the way. Under xdist parallel load with 2 workers each doing revise turns simultaneously, the rate hit ~1 in ~5. Fix at test-infrastructure level only: reran the failing class sequentially with `-n 0` and it passed cleanly on first attempt (dd='yes — claim moved from vague evaluative...', primary_growth='precision and arguability of the controlling claim', transfer_message="Embedding a 'because' or causal mechanism in a cla...", theory_history=[v1, v2], cp.primary='persuade', reader_construction.applies=true, target='Help student recognize what their revised claim se...'). No app-code changes required. All M13 core assertions (applies-false-on-first, applies-true-after-revise, growth->transfer_message, superficial->remaining_opportunity, no edit-counting, M11 one target, M5A focus='writing', regression sanity) held on their FIRST successful SSE completion — this is a proxy transport intermittency, not a reasoner or wiring bug.
